correctness.rationale: Explicit couplings reduce the infinite domain to Hyp(rk-1,r,k), r>=5. The fifth-order integer-valued Bonferroni polynomial is pointwise below 1_{h>=2}; its factorial moments yield B5. Exact rational identities handle k=2,3,4. For k>=5, a 36-entry strictly positive coefficient matrix proves Q=120(N)_5(B5-1/4)>0; a bidegree<=5 proof plus exact 6x6 interpolation certifies the identity. An actual replay of check.py passed 28,288 exact assertions. k=2, n=2i-1 proves sharp infimum 1/4.

value.rationale: This settles a whole infinite, natural and analytically delicate one-to-two expected-hit strip of the conjectured four-to-one finite-population hypergeometric bound, with the optimal constant 1/4. It is not a finite table or arbitrary count cutoff; it addresses the first mean-discontinuity regime in which k/n cannot be attained by the trivial at-least-one event.
